# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 20, 2026
**Re:** Lebun Interactive, Inc. / Draibouth Studios LLC: review of the Master Services Agreement and related documents
**Privileged & Confidential: Attorney Work Product**

---

## Executive Summary

I reviewed all nine documents in the folder:

1. Master Services Agreement dated January 15, 2025 (the **MSA**), governed by Delaware law under MSA §17.1.
2. Amendment No. 1 dated October 15, 2026 (the **Amendment**).
3. Quality Agreement.
4. Order Form No. 4 (Thornfall Reckoning), a conformed copy that includes Change Order No. 1.
5. Term Sheet dated November 22, 2024.
6. Service Level Schedule.
7. Data Processing Addendum.
8. Lebun's Austin office lease.
9. Draibouth's certificate of insurance.

I found four substantive issues. Two need action now.

- **Change of control (most urgent).** The Amendment widens the definition of "Competitor" to include any game publisher. Recital B records that Lebun signed a merger agreement with **Fennick Pine Entertainment Holdings, Inc.**, a console and mobile game publisher, on **September 30, 2026**. Once that merger closes, Draibouth will have the right under MSA §15.3 to terminate the MSA and all Order Forms. Draibouth has **not** consented. The Amendment only acknowledges that Draibouth received notice.
- **Thornfall Gold Master rejection (urgent).** The Gold Master Build was delivered on September 1, 2026. The 15-day rejection period closed on **September 16, 2026**. Lebun's rejection letter of September 25, 2026 was therefore nine days late, and the Build is deemed accepted. Lebun's remaining remedy is a warranty claim. On my calculation, the 90-day warranty window closes around **December 15, 2026**.
- **Auto-renewal.** The MSA renews automatically for three-year terms unless notice is given at least 180 days before the term ends. The Term Sheet agreed one-year renewals with a 60-day opt-out.
- **Exclusivity.** The MSA exclusivity is worldwide and covers every service line and every title of Lebun and its Affiliates. The Term Sheet limited it to functional QA of Lebun-published console titles in North America. After the merger, the exclusivity would reach Fennick Pine's titles.

**Order of precedence.** MSA §17.4 ranks the documents as follows: signed amendments first, then the DPA (as to Personal Data), then the MSA, the Order Forms, the Service Level Schedule and the Quality Agreement. Where the Amendment conflicts with the MSA, **the Amendment prevails**. Its broadened "Competitor" definition therefore governs.

---

## Issue 1: Change of control. The Fennick Pine merger triggers Draibouth's termination right

**Location:**
- MSA §15.3 (Change of Control), read with MSA §1.1 (definitions of "Change of Control" and "Competitor").
- Amendment §2.1 (replacement "Competitor" definition), Recital B (the merger) and §3 (notice acknowledgment only).
- MSA §17.4 (order of precedence).

**What the documents say:**
- **The termination right.** MSA §15.3 lets Draibouth terminate the MSA *and all Order Forms* on 30 days' written notice in two cases:
  - Lebun undergoes a Change of Control in which it is "acquired by a Competitor, or merges with or into a Competitor, without Provider's prior written consent"; or
  - the equivalent merger case in the same clause.
- **The original definition was harmless.** As originally drafted, MSA §1.1 limited "Competitor" to providers of outsourced game testing, localization or player-support services. This matches the Term Sheet (§12.3). On that definition a merger with a game publisher would not have triggered §15.3.
- **The Amendment widens it.** Amendment §2.1 deletes that definition. The new limb (b) adds any person or Affiliate that "develops, publishes or distributes interactive entertainment software." Because the Amendment ranks first under MSA §17.4, the new definition controls.
- **The merger is a Change of Control.** Amendment Recital B records that on **September 30, 2026** Lebun entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with **Fennick Pine Entertainment Holdings, Inc.**, described as a publisher of console and mobile games. Lebun will merge with a wholly owned Fennick Pine subsidiary and survive as a wholly owned subsidiary of Fennick Pine. That is a Change of Control under clause (b) of the definition, because Fennick Pine acquires more than 50% of Lebun's voting securities. Lebun is "acquired by a Competitor." The merger subsidiary is also a Competitor, because the definition covers Affiliates.
- **There is no consent.** Amendment §3.1 records only that Draibouth received Lebun's notice of the Merger Agreement under the last sentence of §15.3, and that the notice was timely. Nothing in the Amendment consents to the merger or waives §15.3. Under MSA §17.6, a waiver must be in writing and signed by Draibouth.

**Why it matters for Lebun:**
- When the merger closes, Draibouth can walk away from the whole relationship on 30 days' notice, including Order Form No. 4. That Order Form covers:
  - day-one patch testing for 90 days after launch (OF4 §3.4); and
  - launch live-operations support for 120 days after launch (OF4 §3.5).

  Losing these services in the middle of a launch window would be operationally serious. Lebun's own exclusivity covenant (Issue 4) has meanwhile kept it from building alternative vendor capacity.
- The termination right also gives Draibouth leverage in the open Thornfall dispute (Issue 3) and in any renegotiation.
- The Amendment moved the change-of-control risk sharply against Lebun, departing from the agreed Term Sheet position, and Lebun appears to have received nothing in return.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Before closing**, obtain Draibouth's written consent to the Fennick Pine merger, or a signed waiver of §15.3 for this transaction, in a form that satisfies MSA §17.6.
2. Better still, negotiate a further amendment that restores the original narrow "Competitor" definition. This would bring the definition back into line with Term Sheet §12.3 and would also protect Lebun in any future transaction.
3. Coordinate with M&A counsel on the Merger Agreement:
   - whether Draibouth's consent is a scheduled third-party consent or a closing condition; and
   - what Lebun has disclosed to Fennick Pine about this exposure.
4. As a fallback, prepare a contingency and transition plan. MSA §15.5 gives up to 90 days of transition assistance at Order Form rates, which partly mitigates a termination.

---

## Issue 2: Automatic three-year renewal on 180 days' notice

**Location:**
- MSA §12.2 (Renewal), read with §12.1 (three-year Initial Term from the January 15, 2025 Effective Date).
- MSA §17.3 (notice formalities).
- Term Sheet §4.2.

**What the documents say:**
- MSA §12.2 renews the MSA automatically for "successive three (3) year Renewal Terms" unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal "not less than one hundred eighty (180) days" before the end of the current term.
- Term Sheet §4.2 agreed **one-year** renewal terms, with an opt-out on **60 days'** notice.

**Why it matters for Lebun:**
- The Initial Term ends on or about January 15, 2028. On my calculation, non-renewal notice must be received by about **July 19, 2027**. If Lebun misses that date, it is locked in until about January 2031.
- Lebun has no right to terminate the MSA itself for convenience. MSA §15.1 lets it terminate individual Order Forms only. Non-renewal is therefore Lebun's only clean way out of the MSA.
- The MSA carries the worldwide exclusivity in §3.5 (Issue 4), which applies "during the Term." Each renewal extends that exclusivity by three years.
- MSA §17.3 requires a non-renewal notice to be sent by overnight courier as well as by the other permitted methods. If this formality is missed, the notice may be challenged.
- The Term Sheet is expressly non-binding (Term Sheet §14.1). Lebun therefore has no contractual claim that the MSA should match it. The departure is a basis for renegotiation, not for enforcement.

**Recommended fix:**
1. Ask Draibouth to amend §12.2 to the agreed terms: one-year renewal terms and a 60-day opt-out.
2. Whether or not that succeeds, diarize the non-renewal deadline. I recommend an internal target of **early July 2027**, sent by email **and** overnight courier under §17.3.
3. Consider using the renewal decision as leverage on the exclusivity and change-of-control points.

---

## Issue 3: The Thornfall Reckoning Gold Master rejection was untimely, so the Build is deemed accepted

**Location:**
- Quality Agreement §5.2 (Rejection; Deemed Acceptance), read with QA §2.1 (definition of "Delivery") and §4.4 (Incomplete Delivery).
- Order Form No. 4 §1.3 (Background: delivery on September 1, 2026) and §5.1 (M4 milestone fee).
- MSA §6.2, §6.3, §11.2(b) and §11.3.
- Amendment §4 (Reservation of Rights).

**What the documents say:**
- **Acceptance procedure.** MSA §6.2 makes acceptance of every Deliverable subject to the Quality Agreement procedures and periods. The only exception is where an Order Form expressly provides otherwise. OF4 §6.2 does not; it simply adopts QA §5.
- **The 15-day window.** QA §5.2 lets Lebun reject a Build by written notice "within fifteen (15) days after Delivery." QA §2.2 confirms these are calendar days. If no Rejection Notice is given, the Build is "deemed accepted" on the last day of the period.
- **Delivery date and deadline.** OF4 §1.3 records that Draibouth delivered the Gold Master Build (v1.0.0.4471) with its Delivery Package on **September 1, 2026**. The Rejection Period therefore ended on **September 16, 2026**.
- **The late rejection.** Amendment §4.1 records Lebun's Rejection Letter dated **September 25, 2026**, nine days late. Amendment §4.3 states that nothing in the Amendment extends, tolls or waives any period. Amendment §4.2 and §4.4 only preserve Lebun's position and each party's rights.
- **Effect of deemed acceptance (QA §5.2(a)–(b)):**
  - the M4 Gold Master milestone fee of **$420,000** (OF4 §5.1) became payable; and
  - Lebun's remedies are limited to the warranty remedies in MSA §11.2(b) and §11.3.

**Why it matters for Lebun:**
- Lebun's stated position in Amendment §4.2 is that the Build does not conform and that the fee is not payable. That position is weak on the documents as they stand. Draibouth can invoice the $420,000, and late-payment interest under MSA §5.5 applies to undisputed amounts.
- MSA §6.3 preserves Lebun's warranty rights after deemed acceptance. However, the warranty in MSA §11.2(b) runs for only **90 days after deemed acceptance**. On my calculation that is **December 15, 2026**, less than four weeks from today.
- Under MSA §11.3, if Draibouth fails to cure within 30 days of Lebun's written notice, Lebun may terminate Order Form No. 4 and recover the fees paid for the non-conforming Deliverable.

**Recommended fix:**
1. **Immediately, and in any event well before December 15, 2026:**
   - serve a written warranty notice under MSA §11.2(b) and §11.3 identifying each Defect, by bug database reference where possible;
   - send it by email to Draibouth's quality contact and under MSA §17.3; and
   - expressly reserve Lebun's position that the September 25 letter was effective.
2. Check whether any of the following could support an argument that the period ran from a later date or was satisfied:
   - whether, and when, a QA §4.3 Delivery notice was actually sent, since Delivery occurs when that notice is sent;
   - whether Lebun flagged missing Delivery Package items within three business days, which would postpone Delivery under QA §4.4; and
   - whether any written communication between September 1 and 16, 2026 could qualify as a Rejection Notice.
3. Seek a signed written waiver or extension of the Rejection Period from Draibouth under MSA §17.6. This could form part of a package with the change-of-control consent in Issue 1.
4. Meanwhile, give written notice of a good-faith dispute under MSA §5.3 before any invoice for the M4 fee falls due. Lebun should recognize that the dispute rests mainly on warranty grounds.
5. Preserve any claim for late Delivery against Milestone dates. QA §5.6 preserves this despite deemed acceptance.

---

## Issue 4: Overbroad exclusivity (worldwide, all services, all Affiliate titles)

**Location:**
- MSA §3.5 (Exclusivity), read with the MSA §1.1 definitions of "Covered Services," "Customer Title" and "Affiliate."
- Term Sheet §5.1–5.2.

**What the documents say:**
- **The covenant.** MSA §3.5 bars Lebun, during the Term, from engaging "any third party to perform Covered Services for any Customer Title." It also requires Lebun to cause its Affiliates not to do so, and bars any new internal team created for that purpose. There is no territorial limit.
- **"Covered Services"** covers all services of the type in Schedule A or any Order Form. That includes all testing, localization, translation, community management, player support and live-operations support.
- **"Customer Title"** covers any product on any platform "developed, published, co-published or distributed by Customer or its Affiliates."
- **The Term Sheet scope was much narrower.** Term Sheet §5.1–5.2 limited exclusivity to functional QA testing of Lebun-published **console** titles in **North America** only. It expressly excluded:
  - other testing, localization and live-ops;
  - PC, mobile and online titles;
  - Affiliate titles; and
  - work outside North America.

**Why it matters for Lebun:**
- The covenant shuts Lebun out of the vendor market for every service line, worldwide. It also prevents Lebun from bringing these functions in-house.
- **After the merger, Fennick Pine and its subsidiaries become Lebun's Affiliates.** Their console and mobile titles become "Customer Titles." Lebun would then be required to "cause" its new parent and sister companies to use only Draibouth. Lebun cannot control a parent, so it would likely be in breach from closing. That breach exposes Lebun to termination for cause under MSA §15.2. It also creates a significant integration problem for Fennick Pine.
- Because of the auto-renewal (Issue 2) and the lack of any MSA-level convenience termination, the exclusivity may run until about 2031 or later.
- As with Issue 2, the Term Sheet is non-binding (§14.1). The remedy is renegotiation, not enforcement.

**Recommended fix:**
1. Amend §3.5 and the §1.1 definitions to match the Term Sheet scope: functional QA testing, Lebun-published console titles, North America.
2. At minimum, before closing, carve out:
   - Fennick Pine and its subsidiaries;
   - any after-acquired Affiliate and its titles; and
   - any existing vendor relationships of those entities.
3. Confirm with Lebun whether it currently uses any other vendor or internal team for services that fall within the broad definition. If it does, there may be an existing breach that should be dealt with in the same amendment.

---

## Other Documents Reviewed (no material issues)

- **Service Level Schedule.** Standard service levels and credits; credits are capped at 20% of Monthly Fees and are not Lebun's sole remedy for a material breach. No issue identified.
- **Data Processing Addendum.** An adequate processor regime: CCPA restrictions, 48-hour breach notice, SCCs for transfers, and approved sub-processors in Canada and Ireland. After closing, its Affiliate provisions (§1.3) would extend to any Fennick Pine entity that signs an Order Form. No issue identified.
- **Office Lease.** This is a distractor that does not bear on the Draibouth relationship. For the merger team: Lebun survives as a subsidiary, and under Lease §9.3 a transfer of Tenant's stock is not an assignment, so landlord consent should not be needed.
- **Certificate of Insurance.** The certificate shows coverage that meets MSA §16.1:
  - CGL of $2M/$4M with Lebun as additional insured;
  - tech E&O/cyber of $5M;
  - employer's liability of $1M;
  - umbrella of $5M; and
  - insurers rated A or better.

  The policies expire on **January 1, 2027**. Lebun should diarize to obtain the renewal certificate required by MSA §16.2.

---

## Points I Cannot Resolve From the Documents Alone

1. **Execution.** The signature blocks on every document in the folder, including the Amendment, are blank. I have assumed all documents were executed as dated. We should obtain the signed copies.
2. **Why the "Competitor" definition was widened.** Nothing explains why Lebun agreed to Amendment §2.1, or whether anything was received in return. We should ask the client who negotiated it.
3. **Timing of Draibouth's 90-day election window under §15.3.** The window runs from Draibouth's receipt of notice "of the Change of Control." It is unclear whether that is Lebun's notice of the signed Merger Agreement, already acknowledged in Amendment §3.1, or the closing notice under Amendment §3.2. If it is the former, the window may already be running. The expected closing date is also not in the file.
4. **Merger Agreement terms.** I have not seen the Merger Agreement. In particular, I do not know whether Draibouth's consent is a closing condition or whether Lebun gave a representation about it.
5. **Thornfall delivery facts.** The file does not show:
   - the date of the QA §4.3 Delivery notice;
   - whether the Delivery Package was complete;
   - whether any earlier written rejection-type communications exist;
   - the content of the Rejection Letter;
   - whether the M4 fee has been invoiced or paid; or
   - the commercial release date, which drives the OF4 §3.4/§3.5 service periods.

   I also do not know whether Change Order No. 1, signed September 4, 2026, during the Rejection Period, has any bearing on the Gold Master position.
6. **Exact Initial Term end date.** It is unclear whether the Initial Term ends on January 14 or January 15, 2028. The non-renewal deadline should be calendared conservatively.
7. **Existing vendor use.** It is unknown whether Lebun or its Affiliates currently use other vendors or internal teams for services within the MSA §3.5 exclusivity.

Please let me know if you would like me to draft the consent and waiver request to Draibouth, the warranty notice, or a proposed Amendment No. 2 covering the points above.

## Issue 1: Change of Control and the Broadened "Competitor" Definition

**Location**
- MSA §15.3 (Change of Control termination right)
- MSA §1.1 (original definitions of "Competitor" and "Change of Control")
- Amendment No. 1 §2.1 (replacement definition of "Competitor")
- Amendment No. 1 Recital B (the merger)
- Amendment No. 1 §3 (acknowledgment of notice)
- MSA §17.4 (order of precedence)

**What the documents say**

- **The termination right.** MSA §15.3 allows Draibouth to terminate the MSA *and all Order Forms* on 30 days' written notice if Lebun undergoes a Change of Control in which it "is acquired by a Competitor, or merges with or into a Competitor, without Provider's prior written consent."
- **The original definition.** The MSA defined "Competitor" narrowly, as a provider of outsourced game testing, localization or player-support services. That matched term sheet §12.3. Under it, a sale to a publisher would not have triggered §15.3.
- **The amended definition.** Amendment No. 1 §2.1 deletes that definition. It replaces it with one that also covers any person that "develops, publishes or distributes interactive entertainment software, including video games for console, personal computer, mobile or online platforms." Fennick Pine is a console and mobile game publisher, so it now falls squarely within the definition.
- **The merger is a Change of Control.** On completion, Fennick Pine will own 100% of Lebun. That satisfies limb (b) of the MSA §1.1 definition (acquisition of more than 50% of voting securities), and probably limb (a) as well. The transaction is one in which Lebun "is acquired by a Competitor."
- **No consent.** Amendment No. 1 §3.1 only acknowledges that Draibouth *received* timely notice of the Merger Agreement under the last sentence of §15.3. Nothing in the Amendment gives Draibouth's consent or waives its §15.3 right.
- **The Amendment controls.** Because the Amendment ranks first under §17.4, the broadened definition governs.

**Why it matters for Lebun**

- Draibouth can walk away from the whole relationship on 30 days' notice, at a time when Lebun is closing a merger and is in the middle of a launch. That includes Order Form No. 4, which covers *Thornfall Reckoning* day-one patch testing and 120 days of launch live-operations support.

- The only transition cushion is the 90 days of paid transition assistance in MSA §15.5.
- The termination right also gives Draibouth leverage. It can use the threat of termination to reprice or to extract concessions in other open disputes.
- The Amendment appears to have handed Draibouth this right for no apparent consideration. It also departs from the agreed term sheet position (term sheet §12.3).

**Recommended fix**

1. **Before closing**, obtain a signed written consent and waiver from Draibouth under MSA §§15.3 and 17.6, covering the Fennick Pine merger specifically.
2. Preferably, also negotiate Amendment No. 2 to restore the original narrow "Competitor" definition. This would align the MSA with term sheet §12.3.
3. If Draibouth refuses, Lebun and Fennick Pine should plan for termination. Steps should include:
   - identifying replacement vendors;
   - sequencing closing around the *Thornfall Reckoning* launch window; and
   - preparing to invoke MSA §15.5 transition assistance.
4. Flag the issue to the M&A deal team. It may need to be disclosed in, or affect consents required under, the Merger Agreement.
5. Comply with Amendment No. 1 §3.2, which requires notice to Draibouth within 5 business days after closing.

## Issue 2: Automatic Three-Year Renewal with 180-Day Notice

**Location**
- MSA §12.2 (renewal)
- MSA §12.1 (Initial Term)
- Term Sheet §4.2 (agreed renewal terms)

**What the documents say**

- **Initial Term.** The Initial Term is three years from the January 15, 2025 Effective Date (MSA §12.1), so it ends on or about **January 15, 2028**.
- **Renewal mechanics.** MSA §12.2 renews the MSA automatically for "successive three (3) year Renewal Terms." It does so unless either party gives non-renewal notice "not less than one hundred eighty (180) days" before the end of the current term.
- **What was agreed.** Term sheet §4.2 provided for one-year renewal terms, with an opt-out on 60 days' notice.

**Why it matters for Lebun**

- If Lebun misses the deadline, it is locked in for three more years (to about January 2031). That lock-in carries the overbroad exclusivity in Issue 3.
- Lebun must decide roughly six months ahead. By my calculation, notice must be received no later than about **July 19, 2027**.
- MSA §17.3 requires notices of non-renewal to be sent by overnight courier as well as by the usual method. A defective notice risks an unintended renewal.
- Separately, MSA §15.1 lets Lebun terminate *Order Forms* for convenience. It gives no right to terminate the MSA itself for convenience, so the renewal term cannot easily be shortened once it starts.

**Recommended fix**

1. Seek an amendment conforming §12.2 to the term sheet: one-year renewals and a 60-day opt-out.
2. Note that the term sheet is expressly non-binding (term sheet §14.1). It supports a commercial argument, not a legal entitlement to the agreed terms.
3. Diarize a conservative deadline, for example **early July 2027**, for a decision and for a courier-plus-email non-renewal notice that complies with §17.3. This holds whether or not the clause is renegotiated.
4. Consider bundling this request with the consent request in Issue 1.

---

## Issue 3: Overbroad Exclusivity

**Location**
- MSA §3.5 (exclusivity)
- MSA §1.1 (definitions of "Covered Services," "Customer Title" and "Affiliate")
- Term Sheet §§5.1–5.2 (agreed exclusivity scope)

**What the documents say**

- **The restriction.** MSA §3.5 bars Lebun, and requires it to cause its Affiliates, from engaging any third party to perform Covered Services for any Customer Title. It also bars them from doing that work through any internal team created after the Effective Date for that purpose. There is no territorial limit.
- **"Covered Services"** means all services of the type described in Schedule A or any Order Form. That includes functional, compatibility, compliance, performance and localization testing; translation; community management; player support; and other live-operations support.
- **"Customer Title"** means any product on any platform "developed, published, co-published or distributed by Customer or its Affiliates."
- **The combined effect.** Read together, these provisions impose worldwide exclusivity over every service line, for every title of Lebun and its Affiliates, on every platform.
- **What was agreed.** Term sheet §5.1 limited exclusivity to "functional QA testing of Lebun-published console titles in North America only." Term sheet §5.2 expressly excluded:
  - compatibility, performance and certification testing;
  - localization and live-operations support;
  - PC, mobile and online titles;
  - affiliate titles; and
  - work outside North America.

**Why it matters for Lebun**

- Lebun cannot use other vendors or newly built internal teams for localization, live-ops, PC or mobile work, or work outside North America. The term sheet expressly preserved that freedom.
- **The merger makes this worse.** After closing, Fennick Pine and its subsidiaries will be Lebun's Affiliates, because they control or are under common control with Lebun. Their console and mobile titles would become "Customer Titles."
  - Lebun would then be obliged to "cause" its new parent and sister companies not to use their existing vendors or new internal teams.
  - Lebun, as a subsidiary, cannot practically control its parent. That creates a real risk of breach once closing occurs.
- **The arrangement is one-sided.** Draibouth may terminate on the merger (Issue 1), but Lebun stays bound for as long as the MSA continues.
- **Long-term lock-in.** Combined with the three-year auto-renewal (Issue 2), the restriction could last well into the 2030s.

**Recommended fix**

1. Amend MSA §1.1 and §3.5 to match the term sheet. Exclusivity should be limited to functional QA testing of console titles published by Lebun itself, performed in North America.
2. Expressly carve out Affiliates' titles, including those of Fennick Pine and its subsidiaries, and existing and future internal teams.
3. At a minimum, and before closing, obtain an amendment that:
   - removes the "cause its Affiliates" obligation; and
   - excludes titles of entities that become Affiliates through the Fennick Pine merger.
4. Raise this together with Issues 1 and 2 as a single renegotiation package.

---

## Other Documents Reviewed

- **Service Level Schedule.** No material issues for Lebun. The service credits are not Lebun's sole remedy (SLS §7.4; MSA §7.2), and Chronic Failure is treated as a material breach (SLS §10). Both are customer-favorable.
- **Data Processing Addendum.** Customer-favorable and consistent with the term sheet. There is a 48-hour breach notice, sub-processor approval rights, and a processing-location restriction to the US, Canada and Ireland. - **Certificate of Insurance.** The coverages listed meet or exceed the MSA §16.1 minimums, and Lebun is an additional insured on the CGL policy. All policies **expire January 1, 2027**. Lebun should calendar a request for the renewal certificate required by MSA §16.2.

---

## Matters We Cannot Resolve from the Documents Alone

1. **Signed copies.** All signature blocks in the folder are blank. We need fully executed copies, particularly of Amendment No. 1, to confirm the broadened definition is in force.
